scope: Optional recovery fingerprint microbenchmark only; not official gameplay, Electron OOM resolution or full-world acceptance.
provenance: Retained from the completed six-child-process benchmark output. Writing this report did not rerun the benchmark. The script fixes the then-current HEAD to the exact baseline below.
actualInvocation: PowerShell here-string passed to a Node orchestrator, which ran six isolated node --expose-gc -e child processes. The retained script preserves that measured logic and pins the then-current HEAD.
memoryNotes: heap and rss are bytes at the measured boundary; peakRssKB is the whole isolated child-process high-water mark, including fixture/input setup. Each process used --expose-gc and collected before the timed call.
interpretation: All valid/oversized statuses remain consistent with the old limit. Oversized inputs stop before the tail only in the new implementation.
For numeric arrays the new native replacer costs CPU and reduced the measured process peak only modestly; this is not evidence that the official renderer OOM has been fixed.
The oversized single-string case avoids allocating the rejected complete JSON string and shows a much larger reduction.
These are one-shot Node measurements without confidence intervals. Formal Electron/browser acceptance and sustained-world evidence remain separate.
